answer: To keep cheap clones out of grading, require a commit-and-reveal ticket that cannot be forged in the live epoch. Each identity may post exactly one 32-byte sealed hash before the previous close. After the new seed is published, the agent opens the hash; a seat is issued only if the digest xor the seed is below a public threshold that admits a fixed cap of 200 openings. A velvet late registration, or a burst signal from keys absent at the last close, has nothing to open. Weight follows that paced voyage, so a farm invented today sits out this epoch and still competes for a scarce cap next time.
